content.title: Mariners vs. Angels: Prediction, Lineups, How to Watch (4/3/26)
content.text: The Seattle Mariners (3–4) visit the Los Angeles Angels (3–4) today at Angel Stadium as the AL West rivals kick off a three-game series. The Mariners split their opening four-game set with the Cleveland Guardians and then lost two out of three to the New York Yankees, totaling just five runs against the Bronx Bombers’ elite pitching. George Kirby allowed four runs and five hits over six innings, while Seattle was rendered scoreless by Yankees’ starter Cam Schlittler. The Mariners were able to knock in three runs in the final two innings, including on a two-run single by Cal Raleigh. The Seattle staff has, overall, been solid, entering with a 3.09 ERA. But their offense is another story — at least against the Yankees. Now the Mariners face an Angels team that will look to see if it can win without Jose Soriano on the mound. The right-hander has yet to allow a run in two starts this season and accounts for two of their three wins this season. On Wednesday, the Angels fell to the Chicago Cubs, 6–2, with the bulk of the damage coming off starter Yusei Kikuchi in a five-run second inning. Los Angeles did not respond until the sixth — and those two runs weren’t enough to mount a comeback. Bryan Woo takes the mound for Seattle tonight against Reid Detmers for Los Angeles. Woo impressed in his first outing, limiting the Cleveland Guardians to two runs over six innings, striking out nine. Detmers, meanwhile, lasted just 4.2 innings in his debut against the Houston Astros, giving up three runs and six hits, while striking out nine. Seattle has the edge here on the mound and at the plate. Expect the Mariners to bounce back after being throttled by the Yankees. Final Score Prediction: Seattle Mariners 5, Los Angeles Angels 3 Starting Lineups Seattle Mariners Rob Refsnyder — DH Cal Raleigh — C Julio Rodríguez — CF Josh Naylor — 1B Randy Arozarena — LF Brendan Donovan — 3B J.P.
